LESSON: GUIDED WRITING

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: Writing
Topic 3.9: Guided writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Guided writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we write things down?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify various steps of writing a text
2. write a logical text using the provided guidelines
3. appreciate the role of writing in learning

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GUIDED WRITING
Subject: GERMAN · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Guided writing helps you succeed in GERMAN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GUIDED WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify various steps of writing a text

What this means
In this part you learn to identify various steps of writing a text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify various steps of writing a text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Guided writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify various steps of writing a text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write a logical text using the provided guidelines

What this means
In this part you learn to write a logical text using the provided guidelines. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write a logical text using the provided guidelines.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided writing to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write a logical text using the provided guidelines. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the role of writing in learning

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of writing in learning. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of writing in learning.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of writing in learning. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Guided writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Guided writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify various steps of writing a text)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided writing to a partner. (skill: write a logical text using the provided guidelines)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the role of writing in learning)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Guided writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify various steps of writing a text.
3. Practise this skill: write a logical text using the provided guidelines.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of writing in learning.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Guided writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Guided writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Guided writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we write things down?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Guided writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify various steps of writing a text.
5. Be able to: write a logical text using the provided guidelines.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
